title: Grainshift research weekly — field notes
content:
Purpose and context:
This is the weekly catch-all for the "Grainshift" mini-project — a focused probe into low-bit quantization + lightweight evals for two onboarding candidates (r7-small and r7-medium). Intended audience: applied-ml engineers, infra contacts for serving-runtime, and the onboarding PM. Working doc, rough notes, experiments and next actions.

Attendees / who wrote this:
- Samira Khan (owner) — notes
- Diego Morales — experiment infra and perf traces
- Priya Singh — eval harness and dataset curation
- Luca Moretti — model conversion and quant tool changes

Meeting snapshot (2026-05-18, 14:00 PT)
- Quick sync: status updates + unblock list (15m)
- Deep dive: bitpacking + KV cache interaction (25m)
- Triage: eval regressions on SCALE-100 (20m)

Top-line summary (TL;DR):
- r7-small: 4-bit per-tensor quant (int4 symmetrical) yields ~2.8x RAM reduction, p50 latency up 8–12ms depending on batch; factuality (fact-prec) drops by 2.1 pt on SCALE-100 baseline prompts.
- r7-medium: per-channel int8 asymmetric shows good latency/cost sweetspot (1.6x RAM reduction, negligible fact-prec change).
- KV cache prefetch experiment (prefetch window=8 tokens) reduced p95 latency variance by ~18% for long-history chats but increases average CPU overhead ~6%.
- Two regressions flagged by Priya on QEval-run-052: prompt-type "doc-summarize-long" shows hallucination increases on int4; need to triage whether to reject model variant or adjust fallback routing.

Detailed experiments run this week:
1) Int4 symmetric (per-tensor) conversion pipeline
- Tool: grainshift-quant v0.3 (Luca) on top of runtime-convert flow
- Input: r7-small fp16 baseline -> int4 symmetric with clipping thresh auto-est (L2 calibrator)
- Metrics: model size 380MB -> 135MB, memory residency down 2.8x, p50 latency (1 token gen) baseline 42ms -> 50ms, p95 180ms -> 230ms
- Quality: SCALE-100 fact-prec baseline 87.6 -> 85.5 (drop 2.1) ; ROUGE-L for summarization prompts -3.8 points
- Notes: degradation concentrated on long-context summarization and multi-step reasoning prompts. Short question-answer prompts hold up well. Suspect reached quantization noise on feed-forward layers.

2) Int8 asymmetric (per-channel) for r7-medium
- Tool: runtime-quant + per-channel scaling
- Metrics: size 1.2GB -> 740MB, p50 latency baseline 58ms -> 60ms (negligible), throughput tokens/s improved ~1.15x under 8-wide microbatching. fact-prec delta -0.3 pt (stat not significant).
- Notes: promising candidate for Dedicated tier where memory footprint matters but latency must be preserved.

3) KV cache + prefetch window tests
- Configs: prefetch: off, window=4, window=8
- Workload: simulated user sessions with variable history length (0–2048 tokens) and interleaved tool calls
- Observations: window=8 reduces p95 tail by ~18% on long-history cases (fewer repetitive recomputations). CPU cost rises ~6%; GPU memory load is slightly higher due to staging buffer. Impact on throughput small but beneficial for latency SLOs.
- Action: integrate prefetch toggle into rollout policy for hosted API so we can enable for customers with long-chat use.

4) Eval harness updates (Priya)
- New dataset: SCALE-100 added 120 long-doc summarization examples and 200 multi-step reasoning probes from internal product templates.
- Evals: introduced fact-prec (precision of factual statements per ref), and response-coherence (heuristic trigram overlap penalty)
- Found two failing clusters on int4 variant: (a) hallucinations on temporal facts, (b) truncated completions in multi-tool sequences.

Open issues / blockers:
- Blocker A (infra): runtime-convert (PR #879) has intermittent OOM on 4-bit conversion for layers with fused FFN; Diego to follow up with runtime team (see linked PR).
- Blocker B (eval): need more diverse examples for instruction-tuning distribution shift — current SCALE-100 is biased to doc summarization and misses e2e product flows. Priya to propose additions.
- Blocker C (routing): we lack policy knobs to route user to int8 vs int4 variants based on prompt type. Product/console change required; filed PROBE-432.

Immediate next steps (this sprint):
- Diego: reproduce OOM on smaller repro case; add heap traces and mitigations for fused-FFN layers (due 2026-05-21).
- Luca: add per-channel fallback on top-k critical layers (heads + FFN-1) to hybrid quantize -> target: reduce fact-prec delta to <1pt for r7-small (due 2026-05-25).
- Priya: enlarge SCALE-100 to add 300 product-flow style prompts + 50 temporal-fact checks; re-run QEval (due 2026-05-24).
- Samira: draft rollout policy for hosted API that pins int4 behind canary and route policy by prompt classifier (first draft by 2026-05-26).

Notes from triage (regressions)
- Breakdown: 68% of hallucination cases triggered when prompt length > 1024 tokens and summarization target > 400 tokens. Hypothesis: accumulation of quantization noise in cached KV leading to context misalignment.
- Quick mitigation idea: on detection of long-summary prompts, increase model temp to 0.85 and force int8 fallback for first-pass chunking. Need AB test.

Experiment ideas / future probes (brainstorm)
- Probe: mixed-precision schedule by layer depth — keep attention int8, FFN int4, output projection int8. This might retain reasoning quality with size savings.
- Probe: per-example dynamic fallback — quick classifier at request time to route to int4/int8 based on prompt archetype. Measure cost ROI.
- Probe: bitpacking with soft-clipping instead of hard clipping; test if it reduces long-tail hallucinations.
- Probe: KV prefetch heuristics that consider conversation topic and expected generation length rather than fixed window.

Operational notes (practical)
- Bench harness updated: new microbatcher config (microbatch=8, max-latency-budget=350ms) used for these tests. Config saved to runtime/bench/configs/grainshift-05-2026.yaml (PR to follow).
- Cost calc rough: int4 variant cut GPU memory fraction enough to host 3x sessions per GPU (vs 1.1x baseline), but added CPU overhead may increase host cost by ~5% for hosted API. Net unit-cost improvement ~1.8x (rough). Need more accurate infra model.

Questions for wider team / asks:
- Product: do we want to advertise low-bit variants for Dedicated customers as "memory-optimized" with a caution on long-document summarization quality? (ask: PM Leah).
- SRE/Infra: can we add a runtime flag that disables int4 conversion for fused layers until OOM is resolved? (ask: Marco).
- Observability: add signal for quant-conversion errors and quality-regression alerts tied to SCALE-100; propose tag: quant-grainshift in alerts.

Appendix: quick checklist (do this before any canary rollout)
- [ ] Repro OOM and document stack trace (Diego)
- [ ] Expand eval dataset and re-evaluate (Priya)
- [ ] Implement hybrid per-layer fallback (Luca)
- [ ] Create rollout policy proposal (Samira)
- [ ] Add observability tags & dashboards for fact-prec (Observability team)

Scratchpad / random notes (notes-to-self style):
- Found Slack thread: #quantization: "diego: re: fused FFN OOM — seems related to layout packer; try chunking per-FFN-block"
- PR TODO: add more descriptive metrics to bench logs: token-error-rate, fact-prec per prompt-type, kv-prefetch-hit-rate
- Quick local command used:
  - python convert.py --model r7-small --target int4 --calib l2 --chunk 128 --output /tmp/r7s-int4

End of notes — will merge into weekly digest if nothing conflicting.

-- Samira K.
